headline: Members of Congress convicted of public corruption crimes lose their congressional retirement pensions without waiting for all appeals to end.
what_it_does: This law makes a Member of Congress convicted of a crime related to public corruption ineligible for retirement payments earned through their service as a Member. These payments come from the Civil Service Retirement System or the Federal Employees' Retirement System. Before this law, a Member lost these payments only after a final conviction, meaning after all appeals were used up.

who_it_affects.group: Current and former Members of Congress convicted of public corruption crimes
who_it_affects.how: They become ineligible for retirement payments based on their congressional service once convicted, rather than only after all appeals are finished.
